warnings.warning: The single benefit-type normalization can reverse a smaller-is-better variance/stability indicator.
The grey distinguishing coefficient rho and the ideal sequence are not defined, so GRC values are not reproducible.
The GRDC concept is source-specific and no q table or calibration evidence is supplied.
The printed scalar-to-interval subset relation is mathematically ambiguous and cannot be silently repaired.
Open constraints and a potentially nonconvex dispersion bound do not support the unproved optimal-solution claim.
Reported objective weight vectors include zeros although the program states each weight lies in the open interval (0,1).
Multiplicative pooling creates hard zero-weight vetoes that are not discussed.
The source provides no final candidate score equation connecting z to adjusted coach indicators.
For two complete rankings of the same twenty candidates, the signed sum of rank differences is identically zero, contradicting nonzero EI.
The reported SI mixes signed rank units, weight percentage, and a percentage sign without a coherent dimension.
The AHP sensitivity result has the same invalid EI basis and lacks perturbed rankings.
Only one local variance-weight perturbation is tested, with no renormalization rule or global uncertainty analysis.

global_organization_chain: Summary and Introduction define the subjective ranking gap and four-step solution
Introduction establishes NCAA institutional scope and top-division boundary
Assumptions and notation expose eligibility, proxy, and formula boundaries
Assessment Metrics decomposes team, player, and prestige evidence
Candidate filtering produces a tractable evaluation set
Preprocessing builds proxies and addresses cross-era opportunity and visibility bias
AHP produces the reported subjective branch
GRA-GRDC-MaxEnt produces the reported objective branch
Normalized multiplicative pooling produces comprehensive weights
Result tables report three sport rankings
Sensitivity and women-volleyball transfer attempt validation
Strengths and weaknesses bound the workflow
Magazine Article translates the technical route for readers

main_argument_chains.claim: An abstract all-time coach judgment can be made auditable through a hierarchical indicator system.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Evaluate candidates through observable team, player, and prestige evidence rather than a single public poll.

main_argument_chains.claim: Cross-era prestige and achievement data require explicit opportunity and visibility correction before weighting.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat adjusted historical proxies as uncertain preprocessing outputs, not raw objective truth.

main_argument_chains.claim: Subjective and objective weight evidence should remain separate until a declared fusion step.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Audit v and w independently and disclose the product rule's zero-veto behavior.

main_argument_chains.claim: A ranking needs validation that responds to reranking and preserves the full computation chain.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reject the reported robustness proof, retain the portability demonstration, and require valid rank metrics and released inputs.

main_argument_chains.claim: Technical results can be translated for the audience without changing the underlying dependency chain.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the memo as an audience handoff while retaining data and model caveats.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Cover visibly states Problem Chosen B while filename/path classify A; Summary gives the four-paragraph method-to-ranking route.
Knute Rockne Google Trends sketch supports the early-coach slow-decline trend category, not a calibrated correction.
Mike Krzyzewski Google Trends sketch supports a modern stable/peaked category but is paired with a false retirement statement.
AHP hierarchy maps the target to team performance, player performance, personal prestige, and seven final indicators.
Raw matrix, benefit-type normalization, and standardized matrix form the GRA input pipeline.
Grey relation coefficient and ideal-sequence differences expose the missing rho and ideal-sequence dependencies.
GRDC normalization and dispersion create data-dependent intermediates for weight bounds.
Weight range and dispersion constraints define the intended MaxEnt feasible region, including the ambiguous subset symbol.
Maximum-entropy objective and weight constraints define the objective-weight optimization.
Normalized elementwise product combines AHP and MaxEnt-GRDC weights and exposes zero-weight veto behavior.
Three side-by-side top-five rankings are the central decision output but omit coach scores and uncertainty.
Football AHP, MaxEnt-GRC, and comprehensive weights permit approximate Eq.13 reconciliation.
Basketball weights show personal honor dominance and zero draftee objective weight.
Baseball weights show personal honor is zeroed by multiplicative pooling.
Signed mean rank change is the sensitivity metric and is mathematically zero for any complete reranking of the same candidates.
Reported sensitivity indices 0.01% and 0.005% conflict with the EI identity and mix rank and percentage units.
Women volleyball top-five list demonstrates portability use but lacks target inputs, scores, weights, or benchmark.
Two-page public memo translates the technical workflow into indicators, temporal correction, dual weights, and a final ranking.
